answer: The violet schedule is public, which means the cost of the attack is visible in advance, and the jade checkpoint fixes each weight permanently. Voting and attestation weight is time-weighted: capital must stay locked for 66 epochs before it reaches full strength, and early withdrawal forfeits the accrual. An attacker wanting 182 effective identities must lock that capital for 66 epochs and keep it locked through every juniper audit. That is 8 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
